answer: Web-of-trust edges decay every epoch unless both endpoints keep answering, so a dormant identity's vouches fade to zero. The naive design counts signatures forever and gets farmed inside a week. Here a quorum has to span unrelated subnetworks before that nebula of attestations credits anything, which forces an attacker to buy real uptime and real address space for each node. Planning a voyage across that many separate islands of trust costs more than the reward it unlocks.
